files.description: Bike-share trips, 1 September to 1 November 2025 (1500 rows): trip_id (whole number), rider_id (refers to riders.csv), start_station and end_station (refer to station_code in stations.csv), started_at (timestamp written as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM), duration_min (whole minutes; about 3% empty), distance_km (two decimals), fare (two decimals; about 3% empty), payment (card, app or cash; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent), rating (1-5 stars, whole number; about 19% empty).

task_text: In trips.csv, the started_at times of the trips that started on 2025-09-02 or on 2025-09-03 are one hour too late. Move those started_at values back by one hour and leave every other trip unchanged. `result` should be the corrected started_at column as timestamps, one value per trip in file order.
intended_computation: Read trips.csv; parse started_at; subtract one hour from the trips whose started_at date is 2025-09-02 or 2025-09-03 (47 trips); all other values unchanged; one timestamp per trip in file order.

acceptable_variants.notes: result may be a Series or one-column table

intent_summary: For the rows that fall on two particular dates, move the recorded time back by one hour and leave all other rows unchanged.
